jobs.title: Director, Corporate IT
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking an AI-forward Director, Corporate IT to lead the corporate technology function. This is a full-time role located in the United States.

This leader will oversee IT operations, employee technology, enterprise business applications, integrations, workflow automation, and AI enablement for internal productivity and corporate operations. The role leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for delivering secure, reliable, and intuitive technology experiences across the organization.

The enterprise business applications portfolio includes internal systems supporting People, Finance, Accounting, Legal, Procurement, and Operations. This position requires a leader experienced in modernizing an IT or enterprise technology function through automation, intelligent self-service, AI agents, and integrated business systems, rather than focusing primarily on traditional infrastructure, administration, and ticket resolution.

Responsibilities

Define and execute the strategy and roadmap for corporate IT, integrations, automation, and AI, while establishing enterprise standards for business applications.
Deliver a secure, reliable, and frictionless employee technology experience while evolving IT operations from reactive support toward proactive, automated service delivery.
Partner with organizational leadership to enhance business processes, eliminate manual workflows, and identify high-value automation and AI opportunities.
Lead the evaluation, implementation, governance, and adoption of AI-enabled tools, agents, self-service capabilities, and workflow automation.
Ensure AI and automation solutions incorporate appropriate security, privacy, data access, human oversight, monitoring, and accountability.
Oversee core IT platforms and services, including identity and access management, Google Workspace, endpoint management, networking, collaboration tools, IT service management, and employee lifecycle processes.
Partner with business owners to govern enterprise applications—including HR, finance, accounting, procurement, and related internal systems—ensuring proper integration, security, reliability, lifecycle management, and vendor oversight.
Partner with Security to deploy and operate security technologies, enforce access controls, conduct periodic access reviews, support audits, and maintain secure onboarding and offboarding practices.
Manage the IT and enterprise applications budget, vendors, licensing, service levels, and performance metrics in alignment with broader technology strategy.

Qualifications

8+ years of progressive experience in corporate IT and enterprise technology, including at least 5 years leading teams and cross-functional technology programs.
Experience overseeing core IT platforms and services, including identity and access management, endpoint management, collaboration platforms, networking, IT service management, and employee lifecycle processes.
A proven record of deploying AI agents, copilots, intelligent automation, self-service capabilities, or AI-enabled support into governed production environments, achieving meaningful adoption and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success using low-code, no-code, integration, or workflow technologies to automate processes across multiple systems and business functions.
Experience partnering with business owners to govern internal enterprise applications such as HRIS, ERP, finance and accounting systems, procurement platforms, and business workflow tools.
Experience leading enterprise application implementations, migrations, integrations, or optimization programs.
Strong understanding of APIs, workflow orchestration, data flows, access controls, and application lifecycle management.
Experience partnering with Security to deploy and operate security technologies, manage access controls, conduct access reviews, support audits, and maintain secure onboarding and offboarding processes.
Experience managing IT and enterprise application budgets, vendors, contracts, licensing, service levels, and delivery partners.
Strong business judgment with the ability to communicate technology strategy, value, risks, and tradeoffs to executive leadership.
Demonstrated success leading organizational change and driving adoption of new tools and operating practices.

Benefits

Health and wellness coverage
Retirement benefits
Paid time off and paid holidays
Paid parental leave
Education assistance and professional development

Applicant personal information collected during the recruitment process is subject to applicable California Job Applicant Notice at Collection requirements.

jobs.title: Sr Manager- Operational Technology
jobs.description:
Energy Transfer , recognized by Forbes as one of America's best large employers , is dedicated to responsibly and safely delivering America’s energy . We are driven to inspire our employees to create superior value for our customers, our investors, a sustainable future and giving back to the community where w e have long-standing commitments to causes including MD Anderson Children’s Cancer Hospital, The Salvation Army, The American Red Cross, Ronald McDonald House and many more.

We value all of our employees who make our growth and success possible. We are proud to offer industry leading compensation, comprehensive benefits, 401(k) match with additional profit sharing, PTO and abundant career opportunities.

Come join our award winning over 12,000 strong organization, as we fuel the world and each other!

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Operational Technology (OT) is responsible for the strategic leadership, governance, reliability, cybersecurity, and operational excellence of Energy Transfer's Operational Technology environment across multiple business units, processing facilities, terminals, and pipeline operations. This role provides enterprise leadership for Process Control Networks (PCN), Industrial Control Systems (ICS), SCADA environments, industrial servers, virtualization platforms, and associated OT infrastructure.

The successful candidate will serve as a key liaison between Operations, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise IT to ensure OT systems remain secure, reliable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. This position leads a team of OT professionals while driving strategic initiatives focused on cybersecurity, risk management, infrastructure modernization, operational resilience, and regulatory compliance.

The Senior Manager will provide technical leadership and subject matter expertise for large-scale capital projects, mergers and acquisitions integrations, operational expansions, and cybersecurity initiatives while ensuring adherence to industry best practices and recognized frameworks such as NIST, ISA/IEC 62443, API 1164, and NERC-CIP where applicable.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute the enterprise OT strategy in alignment with Energy Transfer's operational, cybersecurity, and business objectives.
Establish long-term roadmaps for OT infrastructure modernization, lifecycle management, system resiliency, and cybersecurity enhancement.
Partner with executive leadership, operations management, engineering teams, and Enterprise IT to drive OT technology adoption and innovation.
Lead OT governance programs, standards development, and enterprise-wide policy implementation.
Serve as the primary escalation point for critical OT infrastructure, cybersecurity, and operational issues.

Operational Technology Management

Provide overall leadership and management of the OT organization supporting multiple operating regions and facilities.
Lead teams responsible for PCN infrastructure, industrial networking, virtualization environments, Windows server platforms, and OT cybersecurity technologies.
Establish performance metrics, service level objectives, and continuous improvement initiatives for OT operations.
Manage vendor relationships, support agreements, licensing programs, technology contracts, and strategic partnerships.
Ensure standardization of OT architectures across facilities while maintaining operational flexibility and reliability.

Cybersecurity & Risk Management

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Energy Transfer's OT Cybersecurity Program.
Collaborate with Enterprise Cybersecurity teams to implement cybersecurity frameworks and standards across industrial environments.
Establish cybersecurity governance, vulnerability management, threat detection, incident response, and disaster recovery programs for OT systems.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, internal controls, and industry-recognized security frameworks.
Champion cyber risk assessments and mitigation strategies for critical operational assets.

Infrastructure Reliability & Operational Excellence

Drive high availability and reliability initiatives for OT systems supporting 24x7 operations.
Oversee backup, recovery, business continuity, and disaster recovery programs across all OT environments.
Ensure proper lifecycle management and supportability of OT hardware, software, operating systems, and networking infrastructure.
Lead root-cause analysis efforts for critical incidents and oversee implementation of corrective actions.
Support operational readiness activities for new facilities, expansions, and infrastructure upgrades.

Capital Projects & Engineering Support

Serve as OT technical authority for major capital projects, facility expansions, and strategic initiatives.
Ensure all OT and cybersecurity requirements are incorporated throughout project planning, design, construction, commissioning, and startup phases.
Participate in technology evaluations, architecture reviews, and project approval processes.
Provide technical guidance on industrial networking, system integration, virtualization, cloud connectivity, and emerging OT technologies.
Support acquisition integration activities and enterprise technology harmonization efforts.

Leadership & Talent Development

Build, mentor, and develop high-performing OT professionals.
Establish succession planning and employee development strategies.
Foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Promote cross-functional collaboration among Operations, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and IT teams.
Lead organizational change initiatives and technology transformation programs.

Qualifications

Required Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information Systems, or related technical discipline.
Minimum 10+ years of progressive experience supporting Operational Technology, Industrial Control Systems, Process Control Networks, or Industrial Cybersecurity environments.
Minimum 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and enterprise-scale OT programs.
Demonstrated experience leading multi-site OT infrastructure environments supporting critical operations.
Strong knowledge of industrial networking, server infrastructure, virtualization, systems architecture, and cybersecurity best practices.
Proven experience managing complex projects, budgets, vendor relationships, and technology roadmaps.

Technical Qualifications

Operational Technology

Extensive experience supporting and managing:
Process Control Networks (PCN)
Industrial Control Systems (ICS)
SCADA Systems
Distributed Control Systems (DCS)
Industrial Virtualization Platforms
Windows Server Environments
Active Directory and Group Policy
Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Programs

Industrial Networking

Deep understanding of:
TCP/IP
EtherNet/IP
Modbus
Cisco Routing and Switching
EIGRP
OSPF
BGP
RIP v2
HSRP
VRRP
VSS
Network Segmentation
Firewall Architectures
Remote Access Technologies

Cybersecurity

Strong knowledge of:
ISA/IEC 62443
API 1164
NIST Cybersecurity Framework
NIST 800-82
NERC-CIP
Industrial Threat Detection
Vulnerability Management
Incident Response
Risk Assessment Methodologies
Security Monitoring and Compliance Programs

Preferred Qualifications

Experience within midstream, pipeline, natural gas, NGL, crude oil, terminal, petrochemical, or related energy industries.
Experience supporting large-scale industrial operations across geographically dispersed facilities.
Advanced technical certifications such as:
CISSP
GICSP
GIAC Certifications
CCNP
CCIE
Security+
MCSE
Azure Certifications

Experience leading OT digital transformation initiatives.
Familiarity with cloud-connected OT architectures and emerging industrial technologies.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic Vision and Execution
Executive Presence
Organizational Leadership
Business Acumen
Operational Excellence
Cybersecurity Leadership
Stakeholder Management
Change Management
Team Development
Decision Making Under Pressure

Working Conditions

Support of critical 24x7 operational environments.
Periodic on-call responsibility for major incidents and operational emergencies.
Travel up to 25% to Energy Transfer facilities throughout the United States.
Ability to work in industrial environments and comply with all safety requirements and personal protective equipment standards.

jobs.title: Director, IT Applications
jobs.description:
Drive Technology Innovation and Build High-Performing Teams at Liberty Dental Plan

Are you a strategic technology leader who excels at developing people, partnering with the business, and delivering enterprise applications that drive measurable results? Liberty Dental Plan is seeking a Director, IT Applications
to lead a critical portfolio of business applications while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Reporting to the VP, Application Development
, this highly visible leadership role combines technology strategy, operational excellence, and people leadership. You will help shape the future of our application landscape, strengthen business partnerships, and guide a talented team responsible for delivering reliable, secure, and scalable solutions that support our members, clients, and organization.

About The Role

The Director, IT Applications is responsible for leading the delivery, support, maintenance, and ongoing evolution of enterprise applications across assigned business areas. This role ensures applications meet business needs, service level commitments, quality standards, and security requirements while supporting operational performance and organizational growth.

The ideal candidate brings a combination of healthcare payer industry knowledge, strong people leadership capabilities, business acumen, and experience managing vendor relationships and enterprise application portfolios.

Location:
Remote

Reporting Relationship:
VP, Application Development

What You'll Do

Technology Strategy & Application Leadership

Lead the delivery, support, maintenance, and optimization of critical business applications.
Serve as the product owner for assigned application platforms, establishing strategic priorities, modernization initiatives, and technology roadmaps.
Partner with business leaders to understand requirements, identify process bottlenecks, and recommend technology solutions that improve efficiency and productivity.
Balance business priorities, operational stability, modernization efforts, and technical debt reduction.
Guide application strategy and influence technical direction in partnership with technical teams and stakeholders.

Operational Excellence

Ensure applications meet agreed-upon service level expectations for availability, performance, incident response, and production support.
Oversee release planning, production readiness, ongoing maintenance, and enhancement activities.
Maintain strong controls around data integrity, compliance, security, and system management.
Monitor application health, technical debt, and remediation efforts while communicating risks and progress to leadership.
Identify and proactively address operational and delivery risks to ensure successful outcomes.
Support audits, client reviews, regulatory inquiries, proposal responses, and new client implementation activities.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with vendors, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
Manage third-party resources and consulting relationships to support delivery and operational objectives.
Partner with compliance, security, infrastructure, architecture, governance, and business operations teams to ensure alignment and execution.
Navigate competing priorities effectively while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships and transparency.

People & Team Leadership

Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technology professionals.
Create an environment where employees feel supported, empowered, and accountable for results.
Establish clear expectations and provide ongoing performance feedback and development opportunities.
Foster collaboration, trust, continuous learning, and professional growth.
Delegate effectively while developing future leaders and building organizational capability.
Recognize and celebrate team contributions while maintaining a high-performance culture.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in IT applications, application support, systems delivery, or a related discipline.
5+ years of people leadership experience.
Strong understanding of application delivery, support, operations, and service level management.
Experience with software development lifecycles, release management, production support, and application maintenance practices.
Experience managing vendors, budgets, resources, operational risks, and delivery governance.
Ability to build trusted relationships with business leaders, technical teams, and external partners.
Strong communication, problem-solving, decision-making, and leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Healthcare payer experience, including Medicare and/or Medicaid environments.
Dental payer experience strongly preferred.
Experience supporting delegated healthcare models and healthcare operations.
Experience with Health Solutions Plus (HSP) and healthcare payer administration platforms highly preferred.
Experience participating in audits, regulatory reviews, RFP responses, and client-facing initiatives.
Experience with Agile delivery methodologies.
Familiarity with Azure, APIs, web portals, management information systems, and database technologies.
Experience collaborating with Scrum Masters and Project Managers.
Experience with DevOps practices and modern application delivery approaches.
Previous experience working with Conduent or similar healthcare technology partners is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Successful candidates will be able to:

Build strong partnerships across business and technology teams.
Develop and retain engaged, high-performing employees.
Deliver reliable, secure, and business-focused technology solutions.
Balance competing priorities while maintaining operational excellence.
Drive innovation and modernization without losing focus on stability and service quality.
Lead with integrity, sound judgment, and a commitment to organizational success.

Why Join Liberty Dental Plan?

At Liberty Dental Plan, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can grow professionally, contribute meaningfully, and make an impact. You'll join a collaborative organization where leadership is measured not only by results, but by the ability to develop talent, strengthen relationships, inspire innovation, and create lasting business value.

As the Director, IT Applications, you'll have the opportunity to influence enterprise technology strategy, lead meaningful transformation initiatives, mentor future leaders, and help advance solutions that support the health and well-being of the communities we serve.

Ready to make a lasting impact? Apply today and help shape the future of technology at Liberty Dental Plan.

Qualifications

Location

Our employees are distributed in office locations in multiple markets across the United States. We are unable to hire or allow employees to work outside of the United States.

What Liberty Offers

Happy, healthy employees enhance our ability to assist our members and contribute more actively to their communities. That’s why Liberty offers competitive and attractive benefit packages for our employees. We strive to care for employees in ways that promote wellness and productivity.

Our first-class benefits package supports employees and their dependents with:

Competitive pay structure and savings options to help you reach your financial goals.
Excellent 401(k) retirement benefits, including employer match, Roth IRA options, immediate vesting during the Safe Harbor period, and access to professional financial advice through Financial Engines.
Affordable medical insurance, with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage. Liberty subsidizes the cost for eligible dependents enrolled in the plan.
100% employer-paid dental coverage for employees and eligible dependents.
Vision insurance with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage and dependents.
Company-paid basic life and AD&D insurance, equal to one times your base salary, with options to purchase additional supplemental coverage.
Flexible Spending Accounts for healthcare and dependent care expenses.
Voluntary benefit programs, including accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance.
Long-term disability coverage.
Expansive wellness programs, including company-wide wellness challenges, BurnAlong memberships, and gym discounts.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) to support mental health and well-being.
Generous vacation and sick leave policies, with the ability to roll over unused time.
10 paid company holidays.
Tuition reimbursement for eligible educational expenses.
Remote or hybrid work options available for various positions.

Compensation

In the spirit of pay transparency, the base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $200,000 a year,
not including fringe benefits or potential bonuses. At Liberty, your final base salary will be determined by factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and experience. We are committed to pay equity and also consider the internal equity of our current team members when making final compensation decisions.

Please note that the range listed represents the full base salary range for this role. Typically, offers are not made at the top of the range to allow for future salary growth.

Liberty Dental Plan commits to maintaining a work environment that acknowledges all individuals within the workplace and will continue to engage in practices that are inclusive of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We strive to have every person within the organization have a sense of belonging while encouraging individuals to unleash their full potential. Liberty will leverage diverse perspectives in building high performance teams and organizational culture.

Liberty Dental Plan will continue to strengthen and develop external partnerships by providing equitable health care access and improving population health in the communities we serve.

We comply with all applicable laws and regulations on non-discrimination in employment, recruitment, promotions, and transfers, as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements.

Sponsorship and Relocation Specifications

Liberty Dental Plan is an Equal Opportunity Employer / VETS / Disabled.

No relocation assistance or sponsorship available at this time.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Director of Information Technology
will oversee the internal technology estate end to end and lead the team responsible for running it. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, this full-time role based in the United States covers identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, service management, and the internal artificial intelligence platform across a distributed, remote-first organization.

This position is designed for a leader experienced in building and scaling internal technology through periods of rapid growth, possessing the capability to construct a multi-year roadmap while maintaining the ability to resolve operational issues directly. The role collaborates closely with Security, Engineering, Finance, and Human Resources leadership while managing vendor and managed service provider relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Build and execute a multi-year internal technology roadmap across identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, and service management.
Tie technology investments directly to business outcomes with defined success measures.
Define internal delivery models versus services managed through partners and managed service providers.
Establish IT governance, operating standards, architecture reviews, and change management.
Design the internal IT function, build business cases for headcount, and hire and develop team members.
Mentor the team and establish clear ownership, on-call schedules, and escalation models.
Build and maintain the internal service catalog and associated service level agreements.
Own internal AI tool use case development, rollout, training, and adoption measurement.
Partner with the organization's AI practice so internal usage directly informs client-facing delivery.
Apply financial engineering to the internal AI estate by developing unit-cost models, forecasting consumption, negotiating commitments and reserved capacity, and holding AI expenditures accountable to measured productivity gains.
Own endpoint management, configuration baselines, patching, and hardware lifecycles using Intune or equivalent systems.
Manage the Microsoft 365 collaboration environment, including Teams, SharePoint, and Exchange governance.
Define and enforce device posture requirements for a remote-first workforce.
Direct internal network architecture, remote access, and secure connectivity models.
Manage the internal cloud and hosting footprint, including capacity, cost, and resilience.
Direct backup, recovery, and business continuity for internal systems with tested recovery objectives.
Establish and mature IT service management across intake, incident, problem, request, and change processes.
Publish operational metrics and systematically eliminate key sources of employee workflow friction.
Oversee the onboarding and offboarding technology experience in partnership with Human Resources.
Manage the internal IT budget, financial forecasts, and software licensing positions.
Rationalize the SaaS estate and direct renewals, contract negotiations, and vendor terms.
Hold external partners and managed service providers accountable to defined service levels.
Partner with security leadership to execute the IT components of the broader security program.
Support SOC 2 and ISO audit readiness, including control operation and evidence collection.
Own vulnerability management and remediation across internal systems and endpoints.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of information technology experience, including proven experience leading teams or owning a technology function.
Demonstrated experience building and scaling internal IT within a distributed or remote-first company during periods of rapid growth.
Experience presenting technology strategy, investment recommendations, operational risks, and performance metrics to executive leadership.
Deep hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint management (Intune or equivalent), and SaaS administration at scale.
Demonstrated ownership of internal AI adoption and governance, including policy creation, data handling, and change management.
Strong security fluency, with the ability to partner credibly with executive security leadership and translate technical risk into business terms.
Proven experience supporting SOC 2, ISO, or related regulated compliance and audit requirements.
Experience managing IT budgets and negotiating contracts with vendors and managed service providers.
Ability to communicate technical trade-offs clearly to both executive and technical audiences, in writing and in person.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience operating within a solutions provider, managed service provider (MSP), or technology consulting environment.
Relevant industry certifications, such as ITIL, Microsoft certifications, CISSP, CISM, PMP, or equivalent credentials.

Compensation and Benefits

Full-time employment status.
Discretionary incentive compensation and bonus opportunities based on individual and organizational performance.
Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with an employer match.
Flexible time off, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Short-term and long-term disability insurance.
Life insurance.
Paid parental leave.

Employment Notices

The organization is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. Qualified candidates are considered without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, final compensation is determined based on experience, skills, and location. jobs.title: Sr. Director, Technology & Systems
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr. Director, Technology & Systems based in the United States.

This is a senior technology leadership opportunity to build the systems foundation supporting a growing, mission-driven organization.

The role owns technology strategy end-to-end, from multi-year roadmaps and infrastructure to data governance, cybersecurity, vendors, and technology investments.

You will serve as the organization’s trusted technology advisor, helping executive and departmental leaders make smart, scalable decisions.

A major focus will be identifying practical opportunities for AI to increase organizational capacity while ensuring responsible adoption, training, and appropriate safeguards.

The position combines strategic leadership with hands-on oversight of systems, vendors, projects, budgets, and organizational change.

You will lead and develop internal technology capabilities while working closely with external partners and cross-functional stakeholders.

For an experienced technology leader seeking meaningful scope, executive visibility, and the opportunity to build sustainable systems for a purpose-driven organization, this role offers significant impact.

Accountabilities

Own the multi-year technology strategy and roadmap, translating organizational growth objectives into a scalable systems and infrastructure plan.
Serve as the internal authority on technology investments, implementations, priorities, and trade-offs, providing clear recommendations to executive leadership.
Evaluate the technology environment end-to-end and sequence investments to support sustainable growth rather than fragmented or reactive solutions.
Manage the technology budget across vendors, licenses, staffing, infrastructure, and strategic projects with strong fiscal accountability.
Establish organization-wide standards for technology evaluation, procurement, implementation, and governance.
Report on technology performance, risks, priorities, and roadmap progress to senior leadership and the Board when appropriate.
Advise Program and Development leaders on data governance, CRM strategy, cybersecurity, and technology solutions aligned with their operational needs.
Establish consistent data standards and governance practices across Program, Development, Finance, and other core systems.
Define cybersecurity policies and ensure internal teams and external vendors meet expectations for training, access management, security, and incident response.
Manage relationships with retained IT providers, technology vendors, consultants, and other external partners, establishing KPIs and accountability for service quality, security, and value.
Lead RFP, vendor selection, contract negotiation, and technology procurement processes.
Oversee IT infrastructure and support, including cloud collaboration environments, hardware, access management, and business continuity.
Continuously assess the appropriate balance between internal technology capabilities and external vendor support.
Lead the responsible adoption of AI across the organization, identifying high-value use cases while establishing clear boundaries around appropriate usage.
Develop AI training, change management, usage policies, and risk guardrails to support effective and responsible adoption.
Lead organizational change initiatives for new systems and processes, ensuring solutions are embraced and effectively used across departments.
Coach and develop direct reports while building broader internal technology capabilities and reducing reliance on individual knowledge.
Translate complex technical decisions into practical business terms that non-technical leaders can understand, act on, and support.

Requirements

8–10+ years of experience in technology or systems leadership, including 3–5+ years at a senior or director level owning technology strategy in a nonprofit, scaling organization, or comparable environment.
Demonstrated project management experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives with competing priorities and timelines through successful completion.
Strong vendor and contract management experience, including RFPs, technology procurement, consultant selection, and negotiations.
Experience with CRM platforms such as Salesforce, Blackbaud, or equivalent systems, as well as cloud collaboration environments such as Microsoft 365.
Hands-on experience evaluating and deploying AI tools in an organizational environment, including adoption, training, governance, and risk management.
Proven ability to lead technology strategy across functions and translate technical decisions into actionable recommendations for non-technical leaders.
Working knowledge of data governance, cybersecurity policies, standards, access management, and incident response practices.
Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to manage upward, downward, and across complex organizations while coordinating internal employees and external partners.
Intellectual curiosity and a commitment to staying current with emerging technology, AI capabilities, and modern systems practices.
Strong executive presence and communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations and technology strategy to senior leadership and Board-level stakeholders.
Highly organized, deadline-driven, and capable of managing multiple high-priority initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, constituent, and business data.
Strong alignment with mission-driven work and enthusiasm for communicating organizational values, purpose, and priorities.
Commitment to advancing equity, inclusion, trust, and belonging across technology strategy and organizational operations.
Preferred experience with Claude or comparable AI platforms, enterprise-scale software deployments, and security or project management certifications such as CISSP or PMP.
Strong ownership, adaptability, prioritization, collaboration, and relationship-building skills, with a focus on sustainable and scalable solutions.

Benefits

Annual salary of $165,000–$190,000.
Eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus.
Employer-paid health insurance premiums, with dependent coverage available at additional cost.
403(b) retirement plan with an employer match of up to 3%.
Fully remote position based in the greater Los Angeles area, with occasional in-person meetings and events.
Relocation assistance available for candidates relocating to the Los Angeles area.
Opportunity to shape technology strategy and infrastructure across a growing, mission-driven organization.
Significant executive visibility and direct influence over technology investments, systems, AI adoption, cybersecurity, and organizational change.
Leadership responsibility spanning internal technology staff, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Opportunity to build scalable systems, strengthen organizational capabilities, and introduce responsible AI solutions with measurable impact.
Equal opportunity workplace with accommodations available throughout the hiring and employment process.

How Jobgether Works

new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr. Director, Technology & Systems based in the United States.

This is a senior technology leadership opportunity to build the systems foundation supporting a growing, mission-driven organization.

The role owns technology strategy end-to-end, from multi-year roadmaps and infrastructure to data governance, cybersecurity, vendors, and technology investments.

You will serve as the organization’s trusted technology advisor, helping executive and departmental leaders make smart, scalable decisions.

A major focus will be identifying practical opportunities for AI to increase organizational capacity while ensuring responsible adoption, training, and appropriate safeguards.

The position combines strategic leadership with hands-on oversight of systems, vendors, projects, budgets, and organizational change.

You will lead and develop internal technology capabilities while working closely with external partners and cross-functional stakeholders.

For an experienced technology leader seeking meaningful scope, executive visibility, and the opportunity to build sustainable systems for a purpose-driven organization, this role offers significant impact.

Accountabilities

Own the multi-year technology strategy and roadmap, translating organizational growth objectives into a scalable systems and infrastructure plan.
Serve as the internal authority on technology investments, implementations, priorities, and trade-offs, providing clear recommendations to executive leadership.
Evaluate the technology environment end-to-end and sequence investments to support sustainable growth rather than fragmented or reactive solutions.
Manage the technology budget across vendors, licenses, staffing, infrastructure, and strategic projects with strong fiscal accountability.
Establish organization-wide standards for technology evaluation, procurement, implementation, and governance.
Report on technology performance, risks, priorities, and roadmap progress to senior leadership and the Board when appropriate.
Advise Program and Development leaders on data governance, CRM strategy, cybersecurity, and technology solutions aligned with their operational needs.
Establish consistent data standards and governance practices across Program, Development, Finance, and other core systems.
Define cybersecurity policies and ensure internal teams and external vendors meet expectations for training, access management, security, and incident response.
Manage relationships with retained IT providers, technology vendors, consultants, and other external partners, establishing KPIs and accountability for service quality, security, and value.
Lead RFP, vendor selection, contract negotiation, and technology procurement processes.
Oversee IT infrastructure and support, including cloud collaboration environments, hardware, access management, and business continuity.
Continuously assess the appropriate balance between internal technology capabilities and external vendor support.
Lead the responsible adoption of AI across the organization, identifying high-value use cases while establishing clear boundaries around appropriate usage.
Develop AI training, change management, usage policies, and risk guardrails to support effective and responsible adoption.
Lead organizational change initiatives for new systems and processes, ensuring solutions are embraced and effectively used across departments.
Coach and develop direct reports while building broader internal technology capabilities and reducing reliance on individual knowledge.
Translate complex technical decisions into practical business terms that non-technical leaders can understand, act on, and support.

Requirements

8–10+ years of experience in technology or systems leadership, including 3–5+ years at a senior or director level owning technology strategy in a nonprofit, scaling organization, or comparable environment.
Demonstrated project management experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives with competing priorities and timelines through successful completion.
Strong vendor and contract management experience, including RFPs, technology procurement, consultant selection, and negotiations.
Experience with CRM platforms such as Salesforce, Blackbaud, or equivalent systems, as well as cloud collaboration environments such as Microsoft 365.
Hands-on experience evaluating and deploying AI tools in an organizational environment, including adoption, training, governance, and risk management.
Proven ability to lead technology strategy across functions and translate technical decisions into actionable recommendations for non-technical leaders.
Working knowledge of data governance, cybersecurity policies, standards, access management, and incident response practices.
Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to manage upward, downward, and across complex organizations while coordinating internal employees and external partners.
Intellectual curiosity and a commitment to staying current with emerging technology, AI capabilities, and modern systems practices.
Strong executive presence and communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations and technology strategy to senior leadership and Board-level stakeholders.
Highly organized, deadline-driven, and capable of managing multiple high-priority initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, constituent, and business data.
Strong alignment with mission-driven work and enthusiasm for communicating organizational values, purpose, and priorities.
Commitment to advancing equity, inclusion, trust, and belonging across technology strategy and organizational operations.
Preferred experience with Claude or comparable AI platforms, enterprise-scale software deployments, and security or project management certifications such as CISSP or PMP.
Strong ownership, adaptability, prioritization, collaboration, and relationship-building skills, with a focus on sustainable and scalable solutions.

Benefits

Annual salary of $165,000–$190,000.
Eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus.
Employer-paid health insurance premiums, with dependent coverage available at additional cost.
403(b) retirement plan with an employer match of up to 3%.
Fully remote position based in the greater Los Angeles area, with occasional in-person meetings and events.
Relocation assistance available for candidates relocating to the Los Angeles area.
Opportunity to shape technology strategy and infrastructure across a growing, mission-driven organization.
Significant executive visibility and direct influence over technology investments, systems, AI adoption, cybersecurity, and organizational change.
